__doc: Language-scoped SEMANTIC rules for the fan-out measurement (#1826 step 1b).
These are FIXTURES standing in for customer rules, not a table the engine
consults — the engine enumerates no language anywhere. They exist here for
the same reason detector-fp-repro.js carries LANG_BY_EXT: scoring a
cross-language corpus requires knowing, outside the engine, which language
Every rule below is SEMANTIC on purpose: none of them compiles to a regex,
so none would ever carry a detector. That is the whole population this
measurement is about — 10.102 of 10.918 active rules in production (92,5%)
had nowhere to record their language scope before the scope moved onto the
`extensions` is what the compiler infers from the rule text at save time.
`language` is used ONLY to score a reached file as right- or wrong-language.

rules.title: Keep business logic out of Rails controllers
rules.rule: In our Ruby on Rails controllers, actions must not contain business logic. Move it into a service object or a model method and have the action call it.

rules.title: Use design tokens, never raw colour literals
rules.rule: In our stylesheets, never hardcode a colour value. Reference the design-token variable instead so a theme change lands everywhere at once.

rules.title: No inline secrets in configuration
rules.rule: Our YAML configuration must not carry a literal credential, token or password. Reference an environment variable or the secret store.

rules.title: Vue props must declare a type and a default
rules.rule: Every prop on a Vue single-file component declares an explicit type and, unless it is required, a default value.

rules.title: No commented-out code
rules.rule: Do not leave commented-out code behind. Delete it; version control remembers it.
